title: Sensing and State Estimation: An Overview

contract.reader: A student or engineer with the series geometry and kinematics and only basic probability, who needs to understand how a robot knows where it is
contract.problem: Kinematics and transforms assume known poses, but sensors are indirect, noisy, biased, late and partial; the reader needs a principled way to combine a model with measurements and to state how good the result is
contract.outcome: Describe a belief by mean and covariance; explain predict-update and the Bayes filter; compute a 1D Kalman update and prediction by hand; read the matrix Kalman filter and its assumptions; choose among KF, EKF, UKF and particle filter; apply frames, time stamps, angle wrapping, gating, tuning and initialization
contract.contribution: One hand-checkable corridor example from Gaussian update through prediction to gating and exercises, plus the engineering details that decide whether an estimator works, tied to the series frames material
contract.evidence: Derivations and worked numbers; fusion figure computed from the example; three exercises; Bar-Shalom et al. (2001), Durrant-Whyte and Bailey (2006), Julier and Uhlmann (1997), Kalman (1960), Thrun et al. (2005)
contract.limitations: EKF, UKF, particle filters and SLAM described, not derived; no code; Kalman optimality stated, not proved

findings.location: Section 4 displays (desktop-light-07; mobile-light-13, 15) and Section 5.1 displays (mobile-light-15, 16)
findings.problem: The fused variance P = 0.066 m^2 is hidden at 1280 px; at 360 px the mean and variance updates of Section 4, the measurement model and both covariance equations of the Kalman filter are hidden
findings.whyItMatters: The variance update is what makes estimation more than averaging and the covariance equations are half of the Kalman filter; Exercise 2 starts from the hidden value
findings.action: One equation per line for the three Section 4 displays; in 5.1 put the model equations on separate lines and stack predict and update in one column; keep the heading text of Sections 4, 5, 7.1 and 8 (inbound fragment links)
findings.acceptance: On new captures P = 0.066 m^2 is visible at 1280 px and every listed equation is fully visible at 360 px, light and dark
